headline: NEXGEN ROOK I TARGETS $1.3B ANNUAL CASH FLOW BY 2030 — World's Future Largest Uranium Mine Gets Investor Day Deep-Dive As 88GW Of New Nuclear Builds Global Demand Floor
snippet: NexGen Energy (TSX: NXE) held its 2026 Investor Day on September 1, targeting first ore in Q3 2030 and annual operating cash flow of approximately C$1.3 billion at steady state, with project capital of US$2.2 billion and nameplate production of 30 million pounds of uranium per year — designed to become the world's largest, lowest-cost uranium mine. CEO Leigh Curyer highlighted 88 GW of new nuclear power plant construction underway globally and commitments from 38 nations to triple nuclear generating capacity by 2050 as the structural demand case for the Athabasca Basin asset. Rook I holds the Arrow deposit, the highest-grade undeveloped uranium resource in the world, at a time when spot uranium is trading around $89–90/lb and the industry faces its tightest supply-demand balance in a generation. The Investor Day delivered construction-phase project-level data not previously disclosed in a single document, placing the economics of Rook I in direct comparison to any large-capital resource project globally.

headline: CONTANGO LUCKY SHOT HITS 86 g/t AU OVER 2.45m — Visible Gold In 5 Of 7 Holes As Alaska High-Grade Epithermal Advances 93% Through 6,000m 2026 Program
snippet: Contango Silver & Gold (NYSE MKT: CTGO) released September 2 drill results from the Lucky Shot Gold Project in Alaska's Hatcher Pass district: hole LSS26016 returned 2.45 metres at 86.05 g/t gold, including 0.80 metres at 244.30 g/t, from an extension of the Coleman 3 vein; hole LSS26003 returned 0.50 metres at 81.57 g/t from Coleman 1 Vein. Visible gold was logged in 5 of the 7 holes in the release. The company has now drilled 5,700 metres in 27 holes — 93% of its 6,000-metre 2026 program — with underground development at Lucky Shot targeting completion in Q4 2026, a milestone that would transition the project from drill-stage to near-term producer. At gold above $4,300/oz, the economics of high-grade narrow-vein Alaska gold have rarely been stronger, and the consistency of visible gold across multiple Coleman vein splays is precisely the signal that precedes successful underground resource definition.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT WIDENS TO 46M OZ — $121 To $64 Selloff Creates Structural Opportunity As 762M Oz Cumulative Drawdown Since 2021 Accelerates
snippet: Silver is tracking its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit in 2026, with the Silver Institute projecting a 46.3-million-ounce shortfall — up 15% from 2025's 40.3 Moz gap and accelerating a cumulative drawdown of approximately 762 million ounces since 2021. Silver has fallen from a January 2026 record of $121.79/oz to $64 today — a 47% decline driven entirely by the Fed rate-hike narrative rather than any change in supply-demand fundamentals. The structural constraint is that 72% of primary silver production is extracted as a byproduct of gold, copper, and zinc mining, meaning higher silver prices do not automatically increase supply on any meaningful timeline. With September FOMC odds shifting on weak labour data, the disconnect between silver's spot price and its structural deficit position may be approaching a resolution. Industrial demand from solar panels, EVs, and AI data centre power infrastructure continues to grow secularly regardless of monetary policy.

headline: PETER KRAUTH: SILVER HEADED TO $80-$85 BEFORE YEAR-END — Fed Hike Pause, Sixth-Year Deficit, And Industrial Demand Convergence Justify Price Recovery
snippet: Silver specialist Peter Krauth (Silver Stock Investor) appeared on Money Metals Exchange September 2 projecting silver at $80–85/oz by year-end from the current $64 level — a 25–33% recovery driven by three converging catalysts: a potential Fed rate pause on softening labour data (ADP came in at 38,000 vs 47,000 expected on September 2), the sixth consecutive supply deficit year with an accelerating annual shortfall, and structurally growing industrial demand from solar, EV, and data centre power markets. Krauth frames the current $64 silver price as an extreme sentiment overshoot relative to the demand picture — the kind of divergence that historically resolves sharply when a single macro catalyst shifts positioning. At $64, silver-focused junior explorers and royalty companies are valued against a depressed denominator; the recovery case is not speculative but structural. For silver investors, the ADP/NFP data sequence this week is the near-term trigger to watch.

headline: HORMUZ SULFURIC ACID CRISIS: HOW STRAIT CLOSURE IS QUIETLY HITTING 20% OF GLOBAL COPPER OUTPUT — Acid-Sufficient Jurisdictions Gain Structural Processing Advantage
snippet: Beyond oil, the Strait of Hormuz closure that began February 28, 2026 is generating a sulfuric acid supply crisis that is constraining approximately 20% of global copper production — a consequence receiving far less attention than oil prices. Acid-leach (SX-EW) copper operations require more than one tonne of sulfuric acid per tonne of copper produced; with Hormuz closed to sulfur tankers and China's concurrent acid export ban, global sulfur exports are running approximately 45% below pre-closure levels. Kamoa-Kakula's operations in the DRC provide some regional relief but cannot offset the global shortfall. The systemic effect: copper projects in acid-sufficient jurisdictions — Australia, Canada's B.C. and Yukon, Chile's interior — are gaining a structural processing advantage over Hormuz-dependent operations. For junior explorers, the acid supply map is now part of the due-diligence story on any copper porphyry or VMS discovery.

headline: COPPER AT $6.50 BUT JUNIOR EQUITIES DOWN 34% — Section 232 Tariff Uncertainty And 17-Year Discovery-To-Production Cycle Keep Capital On Sidelines
snippet: Copper has held above $6.50/lb ($14,500/tonne) as LME/COMEX/Shanghai combined exchange inventories sit at just 15 days of global demand, yet leading junior copper equities including Fitzroy Minerals and Marimaca Copper have each fallen approximately 34% over six months — a disconnect that Crux Investor's analysis attributes to three structural factors: Section 232 tariff uncertainty creating jurisdictional risk premiums in U.S.-destined copper, the industry average of 17–18 years from discovery to production (MinEx Consulting data), and 52% of 89 active copper development projects currently stalled on permitting or capital allocation. The bull thesis: when exchange inventory hits genuine emergency levels, institutional capital rotates rapidly and decisively into exploration leverage. Junior copper developers in permitted, established mining districts are positioned to be the primary beneficiaries. For active investors, the current disconnect is the setup — not evidence that the thesis is broken.

headline: TERRA ROSSA GOLD COMMENCES FIRST DRILLING AT VETAS IN 12 YEARS — 5,000m Campaign Tests Real Minera In Colombia's Santander Gold District
snippet: Terra Rossa Gold Corp. (TSXV: TRR) announced September 2 that drilling has commenced at the Vetas Gold Project in Santander, Colombia — the first drill program at the property since 2013. Up to 5,000 metres across 13 holes: eight holes testing the Real Minera target to verify and expand historical mineralization, with additional holes testing broader stockwork gold at depth. The Vetas-California district is an established intrusion-related gold camp in Colombia's eastern cordillera, historically producing from high-grade quartz vein and stockwork systems. At gold above $4,300/oz, the economic threshold for developing intrusion-related vein gold in Colombia has lowered significantly, and projects that were marginal a decade ago at $1,200/oz gold are now entering a new feasibility window. Results from the 2026 program represent the first modern drill data from Vetas and will define the priority targets for any subsequent resource estimate.

headline: CANADIAN GOLDFIELDS COMPLETES INAUGURAL DRILL AT SWAYZE CENTRAL — 6 Holes/1,422m In Abitibi Greenstone Belt; Assays Pending As Soil Grid Delivers 1,808 Samples
snippet: Canadian Goldfields Discovery Corp. (TSXV: CGM) announced September 2 the completion of its inaugural diamond drill program at the Swayze Central Gold Project in Ontario: 6 holes totalling 1,422 metres tested priority targets, with assays pending. A concurrent 1,808-sample soil geochemical grid (100-metre lines at 50-metre intervals) was collected across the property. Swayze Central sits in the Abitibi Subprovince — the geological address responsible for more gold discoveries than any other terrane in the Western Hemisphere — on ground that has never previously been drill-tested. First-ever drilling at underexplored Abitibi ground is the most basic expression of the discovery story: the assay results, expected in coming weeks, will determine whether a virgin target becomes a genuine deposit-scale opportunity.

headline: T2 METALS: 10 g/t AU IN SOIL AT AURORA YUKON — 3,000-Sample Grid Defines Two High-Grade Gold-Copper Drill Targets In Dawson Mining District
snippet: T2 Metals Corp. (TSX-V: TWO) reported September 2 the results of a 3,000-sample soil and auger geochemical survey across its 76-km² Aurora Gold-Silver Project in Yukon's Tombstone Gold Belt, with 1,619 results returning anomalies up to 10 g/t gold, 86 g/t silver, and 0.74% copper alongside elevated arsenic pathfinder signatures characteristic of intrusion-related gold systems. The program identified two untested, high-grade gold-copper drill targets. Aurora was acquired from Shawn Ryan — the prospector whose soil sampling work in the White Gold District produced multiple district-scale discoveries that attracted major M&A attention — a provenance that adds credibility to the target identification methodology. Soil sampling at this density is typically the final pre-drill step; a 2026 or early 2027 drill program announcement is the likely next catalyst. The project is located in the historic Dawson Mining District where orogenic gold systems underlie a region known for placer production.
